newsitem.title: USA: HAWAIIAN AIRLINES Q2 HURT BY WEAK TOURISM.
newsitem.headline: HAWAIIAN AIRLINES Q2 HURT BY WEAK TOURISM.

text.p: Hawaiian Airlines Inc said Thursday that while it reported quarter-to-quarter gains in passengers, revenue passenger miles flown and average load factor during the second quarter, profit margins were lower due to the effects of company efforts to stimulate travel in a weak Hawaiian tourism market.
The company today reported earnings of $1.2 million, or $0.03 a share, versus $1.5 million, or $0.05 in the year-earlier period.

In a statement accompanying the release of second quarter earnings, Paul Casey, chief executive officer, said, "We initiated a more aggressive pricing strategy designed to stimulate Hawaii travel demand, primarily in our long-haul markets. However, our yield -- or revenue per passenger mile -- declined slightly and our increased revenues were offset by higher fuel and maintenance costs."

He added that the airline's prospects should be boosted through a new "code share" marketing agreement with AMR Corp's American Airlines, and a marketing alliance with Continental Airlines and Continental Micronesia, making Hawaiian Airlines their primary interisland carrier.
